issues.description: Constructor signature for class Animal differs between the UML in the problem statement and the provided solution/template. The problem statement UML declares a constructor Animal(String, int) (name and age) (problem_statement.md line 29). The solution implementation defines a single-argument constructor public Animal(String name) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 6). The template's Main.java example usage also constructs animals with a single String (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")) (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 9-11). This mismatch will confuse students about which constructor to implement and may cause compilation/test failures if tests or instructions expect the two-argument constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent constructor design and update all artifacts accordingly. Either: (A) Update problem_statement.md (UML) to specify Animal(String) and remove the age parameter from the UML and any example usages; or (B) Update the template and solution to implement Animal(String, int) (add an age parameter to the constructor) and update all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat), Main.java example usages, and any tests/documentation to pass an int age. Ensure the UML, template examples, solution, and tests all use the same constructor signature.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares an attribute age: int for class Animal (problem_statement.md line 28), but the solution's Animal implementation has only a single field private String name and no age field (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 4). The template/example code (Main.java) also uses single-argument constructors and does not reference an age (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 9-11). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether they must implement and initialize an age field and its getter/setter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute specification consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Remove the 'age: int' attribute from the UML/problem statement and any references to an age-based constructor so the required Animal only has a name; or (B) Add a private int age field to the template and solution Animal class, provide appropriate getter/setter, and update the constructor(s) to accept (String, int). Also update Main.java example usages, subclass constructors, and the UML to reflect the chosen design.
